tweets: Malicious actors can drain Ether from a contract if access controls are missing or insufficient.
This risk often stems from unintentionally exposing initialization functions to the public.
If a function meant for the constructor is wrongly named, its code runs at runtime instead of setup.
Anyone can then call that exposed code to re-initialize the contract and steal funds.
Reviewers should verify that only the constructor executes during deployment and no other init logic remains public.
